instruction:
Work from a terminal with CalculiX 2.21 (`/usr/bin/ccx`).

Problem: a 3D cantilever block 100 mm long, 10 mm wide and 10 mm high is clamped at x = 0 and loaded by a total tip force of -100 N in the y direction at x = 100. Build the solid model and the deck `/home/user/Desktop/solution.inp`:
- structured C3D8 mesh: 40 elements along x, 4 along y and 4 along z (2.5 mm elements; 1025 nodes and 640 elements; node and element ids are yours)
- nodes must lie on the grid x = 0..100, y = 0..10, z = 0..10 with 2.5 mm spacing
- material: E = 210000 MPa, nu = 0.3, one `*Solid Section` covering every element
- boundary: all three dofs fixed on the whole x = 0 face; no other constraints
- load: -100 N total in the y direction (dof 2) at x = 100, divided equally over the 25 tip-face nodes (-4 N each); list the 25 nodes explicitly, one *Cload line per node
- step: `*Static`

CalculiX allows at most 16 entries per data line; split long `*Nset`/`*Elset` lists across multiple lines. Results reach `.dat` through `*Node Print` (which needs an explicit node set).

Submit the job with `/usr/bin/ccx` and produce `/home/user/Desktop/solution.dat`.

Write `/home/user/Desktop/summary.txt` as one number: `tip_uy`, the y displacement of the node at the center of the tip face (x = 100, y = 5, z = 5), in mm.

The evaluator re-solves your deck independently; the reported number must come from your own run.
